roadmap_notes: Original roadmap milestones are preserved in history even when implementation order changes.
VSX configuration evidence was originally targeted for 0.6.2 but was delivered early inside the 0.6.1B Check Point configuration track.

The original 0.6.0B native-backup milestone was deferred pending a rebase; that rebase landed 2026-08-30 as docs/design/BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/design/BACKUP_RECOVERY_CONTRACTS.md (phases RB.0-RB.6). The original constraint stands and is now the design's first principle: configuration evidence is not a recovery backup -- the evidence plane is deliberately redacted and therefore non-restorable, so a separate encrypted recovery plane is required. Backup artifact bytes must never reach output/index.html, the support bundle, or repository metadata; only manifests may be read by other subsystems.
Write/change automation remains outside the current roadmap gate until SEE, VERIFY, TRACE and RECOVER are sufficiently mature.
Future 0.7.xâ€“1.0 major-track numbering is a planning map, not a frozen release commitment; rebase it explicitly when a preceding phase changes implementation order.
DEPLOY.1 pulls the server_data_plane portion of the 1.0 GOVERN track forward to host the living SEE-track platform; it must not be used to bypass the write/change automation gate stated above.

DEV.1 establishes the controlled Corporate Git/Copilot operating baseline; after acceptance, engineering returns to product work at 0.6.1C. DEV.0.3C remains deferred to the pre-server storage-sensitive checkpoint.

0.7.x early VERIFY foundation was delivered ahead of schedule in 0.6.1B.1.5 and 0.6.1B.1.6; the 0.7.x formal track opens with compliance_posture_rulepack_transition promoting those controls to versioned rule packs.
0.6.1C must include the collection execution coordinator foundation (collection_execution_coordinator) before any recurring scheduling or event-driven trigger is activated.

Event-driven webhook intake (event_signal_intake) and passive TI enrichment (passive_ti_enrichment) are gated on 0.8.x TRACE foundations: safe normalized diff, cross-vendor timeline, and the collection coordinator must all be in place first.
Cryptographic posture and PQC readiness (crypto_agility_pqc) is a 0.7.x VERIFY item; it operates on existing CP/PAN configuration evidence without adding new vendors or collectors.
DEPLOY.1A read-only OIDC viewer boundary is a mandatory server acceptance criterion, not an optional hardening step.

Server productization architecture review (2026-08-31): the current Compose topology is a local/single-operator foundation, not an internally exposed product. Before server exposure, require OIDC, strict transport trust, report-only viewer storage, least-privilege containers, migrations/restricted DB roles, secret/KMS custody, off-host recovery and real-environment acceptance. See docs/design/SERVER_PRODUCTIZATION_AND_MODULARIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md.

Large-file modularization is a local, behavior-preserving architectural-health track. Split static/app.js by UI responsibility and call graph, then compose the same single inline report at export time; split main.py and vendor collectors only at tested orchestration/transport/persistence seams. Do not combine an extraction with payload, device-command or UI behavior changes.

Containerization sequencing (2026-08-28 architecture review): the first migration is a single worker container running the existing sequential main.py pipeline with the runtime volume mounted and Nginx serving the static output; per-vendor worker containers (DEV.3.4) are a later optimisation, gated on collection duration becoming a real operational pain (CP was ~180s in the 0.6.1B.1.2 checkpoint) and on the distributed endpoint lock (DEV.3.3).

Non-interactive runtime configuration (DEV.2.1) is a hard precondition for any unattended container: today the only credential/endpoint path is interactive input()/getpass in _build_runtime_config, and --scheduler-once re-enters it. It must land before DEV.3.

output/index.html is a LOCAL OPERATOR SENSITIVE artifact (real device identities, non-secret configuration values); serving it without the DEPLOY.1A viewer boundary is only acceptable on a trusted internal network behind existing access control.

Postgres scope for DEV.3.2/DEV.3.3 is metadata only (scheduler state, run manifests, last-known-good, CAS metadata index, distributed lock); it touches config_evidence, config_storage, config_history, snapshot, run_context and collection_executor. CAS payload blobs remain on a volume. This is one infrastructure checkpoint with its own real-environment gate.

OP.x Controlled Failover is the first OPERATE-theme work; architecture in docs/design/FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md; open decisions tracked in this file's open_decisions. The write-free parts need only a reachable test CP + PAN cluster (a laptop run is sufficient): OP.0 (HA readiness / failover-safety assessment + SCC dashboard, a read-only VERIFY-plane feature) and OP.1 (dry-run plan compiler). OP.2 controlled execution is hard-gated on mature VERIFY/TRACE/RECOVER, the DEPLOY.1A OIDC boundary + an RBAC OPERATE role + full audit, the CP device-interaction-safety audit, the network-device command gate for the new read and write primitives, and a signed change-management / safety review with the network-security leads. OP.2.0 (docs/history/phase/OP_2_0_CONTROLLED_HA_OPERATION_ARCHITECTURE.md) froze the vendor-independent CLASS 2 architecture on 2026-09-04; CLASS 2 stays not implemented and not reachable until the OP.2.C prerequisites are met.

Compliance control assignment, CIS/PCI-DSS/BDDK framework grouping and the coverage/alignment roll-up are designed in docs/design/COMPLIANCE_ASSIGNMENT_AND_FRAMEWORKS.md with an explicit now vs DEPLOY.1 split. 0.7.1 (compliance_control_enrichment) delivers the file-based policy + versioned control catalog + read-only Compliance workbench spine + Overview roll-up - no server. The UI assignment editor and a tagged device registry (compliance_assignment_ui_and_registry) are DEPLOY.1-gated on the app server + DEPLOY.1A OIDC/RBAC + a store.

User-authored compliance checks (the BackBox/Nipper 'define a check: name + evidence + expected pattern -> compliant/not' model) are designed in docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md - all decision points D1-D16 resolved 2026-08-29 (design doc section 10). Phased: CE.1 (compliance_check_engine, target 0.7.3) is a data-driven assertion engine + fail-closed RuntimeRoot check pack (data/state/compliance_checks.json) over ALREADY-collected evidence - no new device command, no server; CE.2 (compliance_check_engine_primitives) adds a curated, individually gate-reviewed read-only command-primitive registry - cp_device_interaction_safety (P0) itself closed 2026-08-25, so the remaining gate is per-primitive review through the network-device command gate plus a real-environment validation gate; CE.3 (compliance_check_engine_ui) adds the UI check editor + signed distributable org packs, DEPLOY.1A OIDC/RBAC + store; CE.4 (compliance_remediation_checks) adds an optional write-capable remediation block, hard-gated on the OP.2 / FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 bar. Arbitrary user-supplied command strings are never executed in any phase. No certification claim.

Product trajectory (owner, 2026-08-29): the stated end-state is a WRITE-CAPABLE device administration platform; current read-only maturity is a deliberate staging phase on SEE->VERIFY->TRACE->RECOVER->OPERATE, not the ceiling. Binding design consequence on every VERIFY-plane design (control catalog, check engine, alignment, crypto posture): shape the models so a future enforce/remediate capability is an ADDITIVE layer, never a rework - e.g. a check reserves an optional remediation block (rejected by the CE.1 validator), the primitive registry is the single chokepoint for a future write primitive (mode:write + the full OP.2 gate stack), and the verify_after re-check reuses the read grammar verbatim. Write/change automation stays outside the roadmap gate until VERIFY/TRACE/RECOVER are mature AND the OP.2-class safety bar is met.
architecture_review_notes: 2026-08-25 architecture review: event-driven webhook, crypto/PQC readiness, DEPLOY.1 OIDC boundary and contextual TI enrichment evaluated for CP/PAN scope.
Vendor scope intentionally limited to Check Point and Palo Alto; no additional vendors will be added at current maturity.
Webhook signal is a read-only collection trigger only; it must never carry collector commands, device credentials or authoritative topology.
TI enrichment operates on normalized findings only; raw configuration, full topology and real IP ranges must not leave the evidence boundary.

2026-08-31 productization review: retain one worker and the static report while moving to the first server. Do not introduce a generic API around main.py, browser-supplied device commands, per-vendor workers, object storage or Kubernetes until a tested operational need appears. Server-only controls are recorded in docs/design/SERVER_PRODUCTIZATION_AND_MODULARIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md.

open_decisions.question: Session/connection continuity tolerance for post-action verification: fixed defaults, or operator-tunable per run? (Originally framed as the auto-rollback trigger; auto-rollback was removed by op_reversal_model on 2026-09-04, so the tolerance now bears only on whether a continuity observation can carry a verdict or a warning.)
options: fixed default (e.g. sessions preserved >= ~90%, zero split-brain)
open_decisions.recommendation: Fixed conservative default once real-cluster calibration exists (sessions preserved >= ~90%, zero split-brain, sync resumed); tunable-within-bounds only after that. Until decided, continuity observations are recorded on the action record and are not verdict-bearing; no numeric tolerance is invented; nothing they show triggers any action.

open_decisions.question: Approve fastapi + uvicorn as an optional dependency set (requirements-console.txt), keeping the core CLI/report path at its current four dependencies?

open_decisions.decision: Cookieless per-launch bearer token in the URL fragment
open_decisions.question: Local authentication model for the console listener.
options: Cookieless per-launch bearer token in the URL fragment
open_decisions.recommendation: Cookieless per-launch bearer token. No cookie means no ambient credential, which makes the local-CSRF class structurally impossible rather than mitigated. 'It is only localhost' is the failure mode, not the control.

open_decisions.question: Provenance vocabulary: add Provenance.CONSOLE = 'console', or reuse 'manual' for UI-triggered runs?
open_decisions.recommendation: Add 'console'. A UI-triggered device action must stay distinguishable from a CLI one in every manifest and audit record; conflating them destroys the audit trail on the first day it matters.

open_decisions.question: Maximum targets per operational-write request during the pilot.
open_decisions.recommendation: 1. The pilot proves the path, not throughput; a per-request ceiling of one makes an accidental multi-device write structurally impossible. Revisit only with real pilot evidence.

open_decisions.question: May the console run on the server before OIDC/RBAC exists?
open_decisions.recommendation: No. Loopback only until the full DEPLOY.1 gate set passes; docker-compose.yml gains no console port mapping in this track.

open_decisions.question: Mandatory operator reason text on every operational-write, and its retention?
options: Mandatory, bounded, redaction-filtered, excluded from the support bundle
open_decisions.recommendation: Mandatory (8-200 chars), filtered through the redaction registry before persistence, never in the support bundle. It is the difference between an audit log and a list of timestamps.

open_decisions.question: May the scheduler policy be edited from the console?
open_decisions.recommendation: No, not in this track. Editing the policy from a browser is a privilege-escalation path into unattended device contact and needs its own gate.

open_decisions.question: Track identity: keep CON.x as its own roadmap track, or fold the work into DEV.x / 0.8.x?
open_decisions.recommendation: Keep CON.x. It is a delivery-surface track spanning several product themes; burying it in an engineering track hides an operator-visible capability from the roadmap.

open_decisions.question: Reported contradiction inside the design parent, raised per AGENTS.md 'Authority hierarchy' rather than silently reconciled. FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md sections 5/7/8 require automatic rollback on a failed or partial transition (and section 6 defines a FAILED_ROLLED_BACK outcome); section 10.1 items 5-7 require explicit human confirmation per action, exactly one action per authorised run, and UNKNOWN as a first-class outcome that is never a reason to re-issue. An automatic rollback fires precisely when the entity's state is unverified, so it is a second CLASS 2 mutation, unconfirmed, against an unknown state. Which text governs?
options: Reversal is a NEW typed CLASS 2 action (own authorization, fresh preflight, confirmation, lock, single submission, verification, audit); automatic rollback and FAILED_ROLLED_BACK are removed from the model
Keep automatic rollback as designed in sections 5/7/8 and narrow section 10.1 items 5-7 accordingly
open_decisions.recommendation: Reversal as a new typed action. The situation an auto-rollback exists to handle is the situation in which the postcondition is unknown, and issuing an unconfirmed second mutation against an unknown state is the worst available action; section 10.1 is also the later, explicitly dated safety contract and is the one the frozen OP.0b.0 CLASS 2 handoff cites. Drafted as principle P12 of docs/history/phase/OP_2_0_CONTROLLED_HA_OPERATION_ARCHITECTURE.md (reviewed 2026-09-04).
open_decisions.decision: Reversal/failback is a NEW typed CLASS 2 action: new authorization, fresh same-workflow preflight, new confirmation, HA-entity lock, one new mutation attempt, independent post-action verification, independent audit record. No automatic rollback for HA failover; FAILED_ROLLED_BACK is not a state. FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.2 records the supersession of its sections 1-8 auto-rollback wording.

open_decisions.question: What happens to an operational HA entity after a CLASS 2 action terminates OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (mutation boundary crossed, postcondition not independently determinable -- including the process-crash-after-submission case, which the product cannot distinguish from a transport timeout after submission)? FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.1 item 7 makes UNKNOWN first-class but does not say what the entity's subsequent state is, and console/jobs.py's existing crash sweep resolves an orphaned running record to 'failed' -- correct for a class 0 collection, and the single most dangerous possible answer for a class 2 action, since it asserts the mutation did not happen from evidence that only proves the process died.
options: Quarantine the HA entity against further CLASS 2 actions until an explicit audited operator acknowledgement; class 0 reads stay permitted; terminal state is never rewritten by a later observation
Allow a new CLASS 2 action once a fresh preflight returns a positive verdict, with no acknowledgement step
open_decisions.recommendation: Quarantine until acknowledged. A green readiness verdict answers 'is the entity safe to act on', not 'did my previous action execute', and letting the first silently clear the second is how a double failover happens. A later class 0 observation appends to the action record and never rewrites its terminal state. Drafted as principle P10 of docs/history/phase/OP_2_0_CONTROLLED_HA_OPERATION_ARCHITECTURE.md (reviewed 2026-09-04).
open_decisions.decision: Quarantine until acknowledged. After the mutation boundary is crossed, process death, worker death, transport timeout or a lost response is OUTCOME_UNKNOWN -- never merely FAILED -- unless independent evidence proves a more specific terminal outcome. The entity stays quarantined (a derived predicate over the unacknowledged OUTCOME_UNKNOWN action record, not a lock or entity state) until an explicit, authorized, audited operator acknowledgement; class 0 reads stay permitted; a later observation appends and never rewrites the terminal state. Class 0's sweep_orphaned_running -> failed stays valid for class 0 only; CLASS 2 does not inherit it.
